newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Government delays Angolan leaders' summit - report.
newsitem.headline: Government delays Angolan leaders' summit - report.

text.p: Talks on an Angolan leaders' summit have been temporarily halted by the government, UNITA's secretary-general said on Friday.

Paulo Gato told state radio in a live broadcast from the former rebel movement's headquarters in Bailundo that further talks on a date and location for the summit had been indefinitely postponed by the government.

Gato said agreement had earlier been reached between the government and UNITA that talks to prepare for the summit, between President Eduardo dos Santos and UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, should be held on September 9.
"Therefore, it was a surprise when we learnt that the government had delayed sine die (indefinitely) the start of a meeting to prepare for the summit," he told the radio.
Savimbi told the United Nations, overseeing the implementation of the peace accord, that he had proposed three dates and locations for the summit to be held before September 20.

Gato said UNITA was still prepared to travel to the capital Luanda for the meeting: "As soon as conditions are right the UNITA delegation can go to Luanda to begin work, so that this summit can happen."
A Western diplomatic source said the government had temporarily halted the talks on a summit until outstanding issues in a peace timetable had been concluded.

"The government has delayed talks until all military issues especially the return of all UNITA generals to Luanda, the disarming of all 62,000 UNITA troops and the handing in of all heavy weapons has been completed," the source told Reuters.

Five of UNITA's top nine generals, including its military chief General Arlindo Chenda Ben Ben, arrived in the government- controlled capital on Monday for integration into the Angolan Armed Forces. The rest are expected to arrive next week.
UNITA is preparing to hand over heavy weapons in two areas at the weekend.
The government and UNITA agreed in 1994 to end two decades of civil war, but implementing the peace accord has been prolonged.
The Angolan government said on Thursday the United Nations Security Council should take steps to press UNITA to speed up its implementation of peace accords.
Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura said Savimbi's refusal last month of an offer of vice presidency in a government of national unity had put obstacles in the country's rocky path to peace.
